threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' instead of the 'Ginger Line' when chatting with locals. Instant giveaway that you're new in Dalston.
Last night on the 196, a guy serenaded the whole bus with a ukulele rendition of 'Wonderwall'—half the passengers joined in. Classic Brixton moment.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I heard a saxophonist jamming outside the Späti at 2 AM, while the kebab shop owner joined in. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can still find spontaneous techno parties in abandoned buildings here, and the atmosphere is somehow different every time.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can always tell by how they react to the BART delays. Locals roll their eyes; newcomers look genuinely confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a street performer on the 47 bus belting opera. Half the riders were into it, the other half looked like they wanted to disappear.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can explore Gràcia in a day, but the real charm is in the little alleys and local bars that take weeks to discover.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the sheer number of closed shops during siesta hours—like a pup lost in a new park.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the Tube' instead of just 'the Overground,' and your eyes widen at how many food spots open till 3 AM.
Heard a guy on the 36 last night bragging about stealing his mate's phone, then spent the rest of the journey texting on it. Classic.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a man serenading pigeons outside Aldi while juggling oranges. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you see a DJ spinning at a bus stop while commuters dance around waiting for buses. It’s the daily schadenfreude show.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they navigate BART delays without even flinching—grabbing a burrito instead of panicking about the time.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the bus this morning while a lady was arguing about her cat being a 'dog person.' Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars in Gràcia serve tapas, but many only do pintxos—better for a quick snack, but they miss the authenticity of the local bars.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their hesitance to use the 'tapa-tapa' method at bars—standing awkwardly instead of squeezing in like a local.
